answer.diagnosis: The forward kernel forms powers and their squares in the input dtype, which can overflow or lose precision before reduction. I am checking the recorded failures and controls before selecting a numerically robust repair.

The failure is dtype-dependent: the wide fp16 case has 23,541 mismatches, while the same-width fp32 control passes. The kernel computes powers and squared powers before widening. A robust repair must also avoid overflow for large finite fp32/bf16 inputs, rather than merely moving the same operations to fp32.

The wide fp16 invocation fails while its fp32 control passes. I am checking the raw case evidence to distinguish overflow in individual powers from overflow during reduction; the earlier raw-reference ID was not directly readable.

The observed wide fp16 failure has 23,541 mismatches, maximum absolute error 6.92785, and no nonfinite outputs; the corresponding fp32 control passes. Low-precision arithmetic before normalization is implicated, though the observations do not identify the exact overflowing intermediate. I am checking allocation and launch details before repairing intermediate precision across the finite fp16/bf16/fp32 input range.

Forward forms powers and squared powers in the input dtype before reduction. This permits rounding and overflow before normalization. Actual poly-02 GPU output has 23,541/32,768 mismatches, maximum absolute error 6.927851837797153, and no nonfinite outputs. The same-width fp32 control poly-03 passes all 32,768 outputs; the smaller fp16 control also passes. These observations implicate intermediate precision but do not establish which intermediate first overflows. Promote forward arithmetic to fp64 before forming powers: even sixth powers of finite fp32/bf16 inputs fit in fp64, whereas promotion to fp32 alone would not cover the stated input range. Accumulate the weighted result in fp64 and retain the existing output store conversion, shape, and input preservation. The backward cache and backward implementation remain unchanged. This prioritizes correctness over throughput; compilation, performance, and held-out correctness could not be verified through the supplied API.
